readiness.primary_reason: Case includes explicit states, target/decoy entities, node regions, hotspot spans, typed objectives, and confidence/clash guardrails; wet-lab construct details can further tighten thresholds.

design_goal.primary: Design a PD-L1-selective scFv focused on an avelumab-like PD-L1 ECD hotspot while rejecting PD-L2 and PD-1 decoys.
design_goal.formal_success_definition: Improve the typed positive-state objectives while suppressing typed negative/decoy objectives, preserving local node confidence, and avoiding severe clashes or unfolding.

positive_signals: PD-L1 contacts are concentrated on the known hotspot spans.
PD-L2 and PD-1 decoy interfaces remain weak.
failure_signals: PD-L2 or PD-1 binding approaches PD-L1 binding.
Contacts move away from the PD-L1 epitope.

benchmark_start.rationale: PD-L1 design starts from generic weak CDRs to test whether AST can discover a PD-L1-selective paratope rather than inherit a tuned binder.
benchmark_start.interpretation: The executable binder segments are intentionally degraded relative to the reference/oracle sequence so evolution has measurable room to improve. The reference sequence is metadata only and is not used as the starting template.

information_gaps: Whether the desired antibody should block PD-1 by binding the PD-1 interface or bind a non-blocking PD-L1 epitope.
Exact mature PD-L1/PD-L2 construct boundaries for assay matching.
Allowed human framework families and developability liabilities.
